sentences.text: All the parties have been served and record of the below Tribunal has been received, therefore, IA No.3359 of 2024 is allowed and the case is taken up.
3. With the consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally.

4. Appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "MV Act") for enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in Claim Case No.2686/2017 passed by the 26th Addl. Member, MACT, Indore by ward dated 9.1.2021,
whereby the amount of Rs.1,44,969/- was awarded to the appellant/claimant towards the compensation.
5.
The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that, on 15.4.2017 at about 5.30 p.m. when the appellant was going from Khandwa to Khargone by his car bearing registration No.MP09-CT-4598.

When he reached near Gowadi Phata, at that time truck bearing registration No.UP78-BT-4339 came very rashly and negligently and dashed the appellant's vehicle, which has been driven by the respondent No.2.
Due to the said accident, appellant has suffered various grievous injuries and his both legs and left hand have been fractured.
He has suffered 50% permanent disability.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the said vehicle and the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3-Insurance Company.
At the time of accident appellant was aged about 38 years and his income was Rs.50,000/- per month.
6. Respondents No.1 & 2 remained ex parte before the trial Court and they did not file any written statement.

7. Respondent No.3 denied all the averments made in the claim petition by submitting that the accident was occurred in the jurisdiction of District Khandwa, therefore, below Tribunal has no jurisdiction for trial of the said case.
It is a case of contributory negligence, therefore, insurance company is not liable for any compensation.

8. The below Tribunal after framing the issues and recording the evidence and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition by passing an award of Rs.1,44,969/-
towards the compensation along with interest of 8% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred by the appellant.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that below Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the annual income of the victim.
More than 2 Lakh Rupees has been expended for the treatment of the appellant.

Appellant remained hospitalized for a period of about 10 days, but no compensation has been awarded towards the pain and suffering, healthy died, attendant, transport,
permanent disability, loss of income, future treatment and future prospects.
Higher multiplier ought to have been applied.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the below Tribunal.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by submitting that the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is just,

sentences.text: proper
and adequate and not deserve for any interference.

11. Counsel for the respondent No.1 contended that at the time of accident his vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance Company, therefore, the Insurance Company is liable for the compensation.
12. I have heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for both the parties and perused the entire record with due care.

13. It is established from the oral and documentary evidence available on record that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle, which was driven by the respondent No.2 and at the time of accident offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.3.
There is nothing on record to establish that there was any breach of insurance policy by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
14. The moot question to be addressed in this appeal preferred by the appellant is, as to whether the tribunal was justified in awarding the compensation of Rs.1,44,969/- to the appellant.

The appellant/claimant Onkar Yadav (PW-1) deposed before the below tribunal that at the time of accident he was working as a Manager in the HDFC Bank, Branch Khategaon and earning salary of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the accident his both the legs, tibia and fibula bone and the humerus bone of the left hand has been fractured and he has been 100% disabled.
His disability certificate is Ex.P/11.

Dr. Ashish Jain (PW- 3) who has examined the appellant, categorically stated that on 23.7.2018 after examination of the x-ray plates he found that the claimant's left clavicle bone had been joined, but his left leg has been permanently foot drop and he has been 51% permanent disabled.

Certificate (Ex.P/11) has been signed by him but Dr. Ashish Jain (PW-3) in his cross-examination categorically admits that in every District a Medical Board is constituted with 3 members along with an Orthopedic Surgeon and after examination done by the three members, permanent disability certificate is issued, but he is not authorized by the State Medical Council to issue such type of certificate.

Therefore, the certificate (Ex.P/11) issued by Dr. Ashish Jain (PW-3) is not acceptable in the evidence and appellant has failed to prove that he has suffered any permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
15. Apart from the above, appellant was remained hospitalized for a period of only 9 days.

Appellant Onkar Yadav (PW-1) categorically admits in his cross-examination that he is still working in the HDFC Bank and Bank is providing medi-claim for all its employees and his employer Bank paid his medical expenses of about Rs.1.25 Lakhs and it was an operation package.
16. From the statement of appellant Onkar Yadav (PW-1), it is proved that he has already claimed his expenses for the treatment from his employer through medi-claim policy.
During the period of his admission in the hospital he got complete salary, therefore, there is no loss of any income.
The below Tribunal has calculated all the treatment expenses of the appellant along with the expenses regarding attender, special diet, transport expenses & pain and suffering.

Therefore, on the basis of Onkar Yadav vs Mohmmad Ajaj Khokar on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95200634/
3 the aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is adequate, just and proper and not deserve for any interference.
